title: Does the Resurrection Actually Prove Christianity?

top_liked.author: @Adam-Morgan4
top_liked.text: I used to look at this more like a debate topic, but after reading Divide Between Two Eternities by Darian Valehart it hit differently… it talks about why the resurrection actually matters in the bigger picture and how everything kind of depends on whether it’s true or not.…

top_liked.author: @kristinafilkova2776
top_liked.text: Also, if it proves Christianity, which version of it? Which branch or denomination? They all contradict each other and disagree with each other..

top_liked.author: @jerrycallender9352
top_liked.text:
'RESURRECTION'?
Resurrection is yet another story contained within 
the World's best-selling collection of fairie tales. 
The dead do NOT 'rise'.

top_liked.author: @somersetcace1
top_liked.text: To put it in its purest form, you can’t use an event to prove a worldview when that worldview is required to interpret the event in the first place. Even granting it for the sake of argument, all the real work still lies ahead, not behind. And that’s ignoring how weak the case…

top_liked.author: @rlionheart8657
top_liked.text: The Undead never last very long. High level necromantic magic is needed to keep the dead animated.

top_liked.author: @sananselmospacescienceodys7308
top_liked.text: Victor Frankenstein was able to reanimate a cadaver but that didn't make him God.    In fact I believe that was the whole point of the novel.

top_liked.author: @BFDT-4
top_liked.text:
What proves ANY kind of Resurrection?

Seriously, what is the definition of any kind of resurrection from being DEAD.

Nothing metaphysical, nothing poetic, nothing figurative.

Go from a body that is DEAD, and then in literally seconds, to ALIVE.

What does that constitute???
